newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France seeks 15 pct cost cuts - head.
newsitem.headline: Air France seeks 15 pct cost cuts - head.

text.p: Air France wants to cut costs by 15 percent over the next three years and match industry growth estimated at 18 percent, chairman Christian Blanc said.

"Over the next three years, we estimate they (European competitors) will reduce costs by 10 percent. That will shape our own efforts: 15 percent lower unit costs in three years," Blanc said in an interview published by the Fondation Saint Simon thinktank.
Air France is due to adopt a new competitiveness plan but no agreement has yet been reached, a company spokeswoman said.
An agreement on the new plan is not expected until the new year, the spokeswoman said.

The current cost differential between the French company and its European rivals is five percent, Blanc said. Air France has already cut costs by 20 percent between 1993 and 1996, due to a three year restructuring and productivity plan.
The new competitiveness plan takes over from the current programme which expires at the end of this year.

"In the three years, the industry should grow 18 percent in volume, on passenger business as well as cargo. Our objective is to stick globally to this growth, by developping more quickly than the industry long and medium-haul routes," he said.
That development would help regain market share and offset a reduction in short-haul business due to increased competition, he said.
The cost reductions would essentially come from holding spending at a constant while the market grows, he said.
